# KelyfOS

> A minimal guest operating system for Firecracker microVMs, whose PID 1 is an MCP server. An agent attached to a sandbox reaches it only through tools: there is no shell login, no SSH, and no network interface at all unless the policy names a domain. Credentials stay on the host and are attached by an egress proxy, so the value never exists inside the guest. Every tool call, every file write and every connection attempt is recorded by the host in a hash-chained log the guest cannot edit.

Single host, no control plane, no hosted service. `kelyfos run` boots one sandbox; `kelyfos team up` boots a declared graph of them with the paths between them enforced by a host broker. Everything is configured by a committed `kelyfos.toml` and flags that may ask for less than it allows, never more.

The reference pages are generated from the source on every commit and CI fails when they disagree with it, so a flag or a key found there exists. The concept pages are written by hand.

Apache-2.0. Single-host developer tool, not a multi-tenant sandbox for hostile code. From v0.9 the VMM runs under the jailer with its own syscall filter proved in force, and everything the guest spawns is confined by Landlock and a syscall refusal list; an agent is still root inside its own guest, and the VM rather than the chroot is the boundary. The threat model below is explicit about which is which.

## Docs

- [KelyfOS](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/README.md): what it is, the quickstart, and the shape of a policy file
- [The compatibility promise](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/compatibility.md): what v1.0 promises will not move, what is explicitly allowed to, and how anything is deprecated before it is removed
- [Upgrading](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/upgrading.md): what breaks between versions and what to do about it — the pre-v0.9 snapshot, the writable trees, and what has never broken
- [Threat model](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/threat-model.md): what is defended and what is not — read before trusting it with anything
- [Resource limits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/resources.md): how much machine an agent gets: units, precedence, and what enforces each cap
- [Egress](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/networking.md): why a sandbox has no NIC by default, what --allow builds, and why there is no DNS
- [Agent teams](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/teams.md): several agents on one host: the schema, the broker, the store, the budget
- [Refusals](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/denials.md): why every refusal names its own fix, and what the ID in brackets is for
- [Flight recorder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/events.md): the audit record: why the host writes it, and what the hash chain proves
- [Host/guest protocol](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/protocol.md): the vsock transport, the port map, and every channel's messages
- [The MCP surface](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/mcp-surface.md): MCP in both directions: kelyfos as a tool for any client, and plugins inside the guest
- [Hardening](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/hardening.md): what a compromised agent can reach, what each layer takes away, and — the longer half — what remains
- [The host syscall filter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/host-seccomp.md): which filter is around the VMM process, how that is proved from the kernel's own copy, and every syscall it permits
- [E2B-compatible shim](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/e2b-shim.md): the REST subset for existing E2B SDK code, and what it deliberately omits
- [Cookbook](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/cookbook.md): complete recipes, each one a script CI runs on a real machine
- [Building on KelyfOS](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/integrating.md): for putting KelyfOS inside something else: the four ways in, orchestrator patterns, and the mistakes people actually make
- [Daily-driver quality of life](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/qol.md): the shell, the diff, pause and resume, port forwarding and notifications — written before the code, with the places the built thing differed marked
- [The policy record](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/policy-record.md): session.policy and team.topology, written before the code: every field, its position in the frozen hash order, which door writes it, and what it omits
- [Retention and erasure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/retention.md): the [sessions] retention_days floor, kelyfos sessions prune, the size warning, and kelyfos sessions erase's replacement-record pattern
- [Mapping the chain to a standard, without adopting it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/otlp.md): how kelyfos log --export-otlp maps a session's chain to OTLP-JSON spans, why the mapping is versioned apart from the flight recorder and never an input to kelyfos verify, and what is deliberately not mapped
- [Documentation map](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/README.md): what every document is, and — deliberately — where each is still thin

## Reference

- [CLI reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/reference/cli.md): every command and flag, with types and defaults
- [kelyfos.toml reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/reference/config.md): every key the policy file takes, and every key it refuses
- [MCP tools](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/reference/tools.md): every tool a guest exposes, with its input schema
- [Event types](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/reference/events.md): every flight-recorder event, with its payload fields
- [Exit codes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/reference/exit-codes.md): what each status the CLI returns means
- [Denials](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/reference/denials.md): every refusal KelyfOS makes, with the fix line each one carries
- [Guest confinement profiles](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/reference/profiles.md): per flavor, the trees a spawned process may write and the syscalls it is refused

## Optional

- [Everything in one file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/llms-full.txt): every page above concatenated, roughly 179k tokens, for a client that would rather spend context than fetch
